messages.author: 2a87862380741ff7
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] troubles to import data
parts:
Dear Karl.

I appreciate if you can advice me about the righ way to analyze my data.

I work with a RIL population. I am worried about my phenotypic data because they don´t exhibit a normal distribution. The pheno traits correspond to disease resistance scale from 1 to 9 so I made a transformation with natural log. I attached you a plot with the corresponding histograms .

I read your book to get experience in R-QTL and I didn´t have troubles to run the commands but I am not clear with kind of analysis is the most convenient to my data (because not normality).

I guess initially is better to make Extended Haley–Knott regression analysis, and then CIM.

I make CIM analysis but in  WinQTLCart2.5. I got some strange results because for example if  I run CIM (model 6, windows size 10, regresion method forward and backward, probability for into and out 0,05, 1000 permutations with significance level 0.05) choosing chr8 and all traits I got 7 QTLs, but if I run the same program with the same parameters but choosing all chr and only one trait I can´t find any qtl. Doctor Basten said that the cofactors should be the same using one or all chromosomes and the results have to be the same.

Thanks in advance for your help....

Luz
